cloze.title: Say it the exam way
cloze.text:
The mass of a galaxy can be estimated from the [[orbital speed|colour]] of the stars within it. This estimate is much [[larger|smaller]] than the mass of the matter we can see. The missing mass is evidence for dark [[matter|energy]].

Gravity acts [[against|with]] the expansion of the Universe. But measurements show that the rate of expansion is [[increasing|decreasing]]. Physicists think this is due to dark [[energy|matter]].

warmup_p2.alt: It has been discovered that the rate of expansion of the universe is increasing. State what physicists think is responsible for this increase. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2018 Section 2 Question 5(c), 1 mark: dark energy.

mc.alt: Measurements of the expansion rate of the Universe lead to the conclusion that the rate of expansion is increasing. Present theory proposes that this is due to: A redshift, B dark matter, C dark energy, D the gravitational force, E cosmic microwave background radiation.
fb: Not this one. Redshift is how we measure that galaxies move away. It is evidence for the expansion, not its cause.
Not this one. Dark matter comes from estimates of galaxy mass. Its gravity would slow the expansion, not speed it up.
Right. An increasing rate of expansion is the evidence for dark energy.
Not this one. Gravity acts against the expansion. On its own it would slow the expansion down.
Not this one. The cosmic microwave background is evidence for the Big Bang. It does not explain why the expansion is speeding up.

mc.alt: A student makes statements about the Universe. I: The force due to gravity acts against the expansion of the Universe. II: Measurements show the rate of expansion of the Universe is increasing. III: The mass of a galaxy can be estimated by the orbital speed of the stars within the galaxy. Which are correct? A I only, B II only, C III only, D I and II only, E I, II and III.
fb: Not this one. I is correct, but it is not the only one. Check II and III against your notes on dark energy and dark matter.
Not this one. II is correct, but so are the others. Gravity does pull against the expansion.
Not this one. III is correct: that is how a galaxy's mass is estimated. But I and II are correct too.
Not this one. I and II are correct, but so is III. The orbital speed of the stars is how a galaxy's mass is estimated.
Right. I: gravity pulls against the expansion. II: the rate of expansion is increasing, the evidence for dark energy. III: a galaxy's mass is estimated from the orbital speed of its stars.

mc.alt: A student makes statements about the expanding Universe. I: The evidence supporting the existence of dark matter comes from estimations of the mass of galaxies. II: The evidence supporting the existence of dark energy comes from the accelerating rate of expansion of the Universe. III: The peak wavelength of radiation emitted by hotter stars is longer than that for cooler stars. Which are correct? A I only, B II only, C III only, D I and II only, E I, II and III.
fb: Not this one. I is correct, but II is correct too: the accelerating expansion is the evidence for dark energy.
Not this one. II is correct, but I is too: dark matter comes from estimates of the mass of galaxies.
Not this one. III is wrong. Hotter stars peak at a shorter wavelength, not a longer one. You meet this in Part 4.
Right. I and II match the evidence for dark matter and dark energy. III is wrong: hotter stars peak at a shorter wavelength. You meet this in Part 4.
Not this one. I and II are correct, but III is wrong. Hotter stars peak at a shorter wavelength (Part 4).
